column4: Visit note | 2025-12-20 09:00 AM | Dr. Shirin Akter, Pulmonology | Patient: Eva Mahmud, 75, female. Mrs. Mahmud presents for her first visit complaining of a sharp chest pain on breathing in along with a cough producing yellow or green sputum. She is a homemaker and mentions that these symptoms began after caring for a sick relative in Tejgaon. She reports no prior similar episodes and has no known comorbidity. On clinical examination, her temperature is 102.6°F, BP 136/86 mmHg, pulse 94 bpm, SpO2 91%, and weight 76 kg. Chest auscultation reveals focal crackles in the right lower zone. Assessment: Community-acquired pneumonia. Plan: a prescription was issued for targeted management. She was advised to rest and drink plenty of fluids, and to return at once if breathing becomes difficult. Follow-up in 3 days for review and a chest X-ray in 6 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 09:30 AM | Dr. Mahmudul Hasan, Cardiology | Patient: Anika Bepari, 79, female. Mrs. Bepari attends for a follow-up visit regarding her ongoing condition, reporting frequent headaches on waking with no other major complaints, following a high reading noted on a pharmacy machine. She works as a madrasa teacher and notes the stress has built up after a demanding month of overtime in Tejgaon. She has no chronic comorbidity. On examination, her BP is 160/106 mmHg, pulse 92 bpm, and weight 59 kg. Heart sounds are normal. Assessment: Essential hypertension. Plan: a prescription was issued to adjust her therapy. She was advised to cut down on salt, pickles, and dried fish, walk 30 minutes daily, and check her blood pressure at home twice a week. Follow-up in 1 month with home blood pressure readings.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 03:00 PM | Dr. Sadia Islam, Dermatology | Patient: Hasan Munshi, 27, male. Mr. Munshi returns for a follow-up visit for his chronic skin concerns, describing troublesome scratching at night and itchy dry patches on his elbows and knees that worsen notably in winter. He works as a call centre agent and explains that his flare flared during the dry winter in Tangail. He has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. On examination, the affected area is about 3 cm across with lichenified plaques, while other vitals show BP 110/79 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, and weight 60 kg. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 03:30 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Karim Molla, 48, male. Mr. Molla comes in for a follow-up review for his persistent upper airway symptoms, noting a constantly blocked nose and snoring with little sneezing, though he previously had itchy eyes and sneezing fits that worsen with dust. He works as a farmer and notes these problems flare each spring in Gulshan. He has no comorbid illnesses. On examination, he experiences about 11 sneezing fits a day, with BP 129/77 mmHg, pulse 79 bpm, and weight 88 kg. Nasal mucosa appears pale and boggy. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 04:00 PM | Dr. Zahid Hasan, Gastroenterology | Patient: Dipak Bose, 70, male. Mr. Bose presents for a follow-up visit, reporting that his symptoms are worse when lying down accompanied by a burning sensation behind the breastbone after meals. He works as a tailor and states his discomfort is worse after weeks of fried snacks at tea stalls in Lalbagh. He has no other comorbidity. On examination, his BMI is 29.3, BP 127/81 mmHg, pulse 73 bpm, and weight 64 kg. Abdominal examination is soft with mild epigastric tenderness. Assessment: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to eat smaller meals, avoid oily and spicy food late at night, and raise the head of the bed. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 04:00 PM | Dr. Habibur Rahman, Orthopedics | Patient: Babul Munshi, 55, male. Mr. Munshi returns for a follow-up visit regarding joint stiffness in the morning for a few minutes, knee pain on the stairs, and a creaking sensation in his knee. He works as a fisherman and mentions his symptoms have been worse since standing all day at a shop in Cox's Bazar. He reports no systemic comorbidity. On examination, his BMI is 30.1, BP 114/82 mmHg, pulse 78 bpm, and weight 79 kg, with crepitus and mild tenderness over both knees. Assessment: Knee osteoarthritis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to do thigh-strengthening exercises daily, lose weight, and avoid squatting and sitting cross-legged on the floor. Follow-up in 6 weeks with physiotherapy.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 04:30 PM | Dr. Towhid Alam, ENT | Patient: Wasim Howlader, 27, male. Mr. Howlader attends a follow-up visit for his allergic symptoms, complaining of itchy eyes and frequent sneezing fits that worsen with dust. He works as a ride-share driver and reports symptoms are worse since road construction began near his home in Tangail. He has no significant comorbidity. On examination, he has about 8 sneezing fits a day, with BP 115/81 mmHg, pulse 81 bpm, and weight 85 kg. Nasal turbinates are congested. Assessment: Allergic rhinitis. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to avoid dust, wear a mask when cleaning, and wash bedding weekly. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-12-20 04:30 PM | Dr. Nazma Begum, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Salma Sultana, 47, female. Mrs. Sultana presents for her first visit with complaints of vaginal itching, thick white discharge, and local soreness. She works as a photographer and notes that the discomfort began during the humid monsoon in Sirajganj. She has no chronic comorbidity. On examination, her random blood glucose is 5.2 mmol/L, BP 120/83 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, and weight 53 kg. Pelvic examination reveals cottage-cheese-like discharge and mucosal erythema. Assessment: Vulvovaginal candidiasis. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to wear cotton underwear, avoid scented soaps, and keep the area dry. Follow-up in 2 weeks if it does not clear.

Visit note | 2025-12-21 03:30 PM | Dr. Asif Mahmud, Dermatology | Patient: Emon Molla, 39, male. Mr. Molla comes in for a follow-up visit regarding itchy dry patches on his elbows and knees, noting that his symptoms are worse in winter and accompanied by severe scratching at night. He works as a journalist and states the rash has been worse since switching to a strong detergent in Cox's Bazar. He has no chronic comorbidity. On examination, the affected area is about 4 cm across, with BP 131/75 mmHg, pulse 80 bpm, and weight 68 kg. Assessment: Atopic eczema. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to use a mild soap, avoid hot baths, and wear cotton clothes. Follow-up in 2 weeks.

Visit note | 2025-12-21 03:30 PM | Dr. Rezaul Karim, Neurology | Patient: Mehnaz Islam, 39, female. Mrs. Islam visits for the first time reporting long hours at a screen and a band-like pressure around her head. She works as a CNG auto-rickshaw driver and mentions the headaches are worse since long daily commutes in Bogura. She has no underlying comorbidity. On examination, her pain score is 4/10, BP 130/79 mmHg, pulse 90 bpm, and weight 69 kg. Neurological exam is otherwise normal. Assessment: Tension-type headache. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to take screen breaks every hour, do neck stretches, and sleep seven hours. Follow-up in 1 month.

Visit note | 2025-12-21 04:00 PM | Dr. Sharmin Akter, Obstetrics and Gynecology | Patient: Rokeya Rahman, 26, female. Ms. Rahman attends for a follow-up visit regarding facial acne and extra hair growth on her face. She works as a lawyer and notices that weight gain has followed her transition to a desk job in Dhanmondi. She has no other medical comorbidity. On examination, her BMI is 31.3, BP 110/85 mmHg, pulse 87 bpm, and weight 75 kg. Clinical findings show mild hirsutism and acne lesions. Assessment: Polycystic ovary syndrome. Plan: a prescription was issued. She was advised to aim for 5% weight loss, exercise 150 minutes a week, and reduce sugary drinks. Follow-up in 3 months.

Visit note | 2025-12-21 04:30 PM | Dr. Saiful Alam, Endocrinology | Patient: Riad Uddin, 65, male. Mr. Uddin presents for a follow-up visit complaining of always feeling cold, feeling slow and tired, and unexplained weight gain. He works as a madrasa teacher and notes these symptoms were found during tests for tiredness after moving to Mymensingh. He has a known comorbidity of Bronchial asthma. On examination, his TSH is 11.7 mIU/L, BP 111/79 mmHg, pulse 70 bpm, and weight 85 kg. Reflexes show delayed relaxation. Assessment: Hypothyroidism. Plan: a prescription was issued. He was advised to keep a regular sleep routine and eat a balanced diet. Follow-up in 6 weeks with a repeat TSH.
